The must-sees

10 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Museum · 1866

    Nationalmuseum

    Nationalmuseum opened in 1866 in a Renaissance Revival building. After a major renovation completed in 2018, it showcases painting, sculpture, and applied arts from the Middle Ages to today.

  2. 02
    Church · 1300

    Riddarholmen Church

    Riddarholmskyrkan began as a Franciscan monastery church. Most Swedish monarchs from the 17th to the 20th century are buried here, under its cast-iron spire.

    Look for

    Along the walls hang painted coats of arms of the Knights of the Order of the Seraphim.

  3. 03
    Palace · 1754

    Royal Palace

    The Royal Palace (Kungliga slottet) stands on Stadsholmen where Tre Kronor castle burned in 1697. Rebuilt in the 18th century in Baroque style, it still houses royal offices, museums, and the daily Changing of the Guard.

    Look for

    On the north side, the curving ramps of Lejonbacken, the Lion Slope, are guarded by bronze lions.

  4. 04
    Museum · 1891

    Skansen

    Founded in 1891 by Artur Hazelius, Skansen preserves historic buildings, crafts, and Nordic animals on Djurgården. It shaped the global open-air museum idea.

    Look for

    Find Seglora church, a red-painted wooden church from the 18th century, moved here from western Sweden.

  5. 05
    Civic building · 1923

    Stockholm City Hall

    Designed by Ragnar Östberg and completed in 1923, City Hall blends National Romantic brickwork with a campanile topped by Sweden’s three crowns. The Blue Hall hosts the Nobel banquet each December.

    Look for

    At the foot of the tower on the waterfront terrace, find the cenotaph of Birger Jarl, traditionally the founder of Stockholm.

  6. 06
    Culture · 1926

    Stockholm Concert Hall

    Ivar Tengbom’s blue Concert Hall opened in 1926. Each December, Nobel laureates receive their medals on its stage before the banquet at City Hall.

    Look for

    In front of the steps stands Carl Milles’ Orpheus fountain, Orpheus playing his lyre among the figures.

  7. 07
    Church · 1306

    Storkyrkan

    Storkyrkan, the Great Church, dates to the 13th century and sits beside the Royal Palace. It has hosted royal weddings and coronations, and holds a carved St George and the Dragon.

    Look for

    Find the Sun Dog Painting, a view of Stockholm in 1535 with strange halos in the sky. Here as a copy, it is the oldest known picture of the city.

  8. 08
    Square

    Stortorget

    In 1520 the Stockholm Bloodbath saw nobles executed here after the Danish king Christian II took the city. Today its painted façades frame cafés and a Christmas market.

    Look for

    On the tall red house, count the white stones set in the facade. Legend says there is one for each victim of the Bloodbath.

  9. 09
    Civic building · 1905

    Swedish Parliament

    The Parliament building on Helgeandsholmen opened in 1905. Guided tours reveal the chamber, and the adjacent Medieval Museum sits under the bridge approaches.

  10. 10
    Museum · 1628

    Vasa Museum

    Vasa sank in Stockholm harbour in 1628 after sailing less than a mile. Raised in 1961, the ship is over 95% original wood and the centerpiece of one of Scandinavia’s most visited museums.

    Look for

    At the bow, find the leaping lion figurehead, the royal symbol of Gustavus Adolphus.
